items.title: Attero to invest ₹3,000 cr to expand critical mineral extraction capacity
items.rss_summary: E-waste recycling company Attero plans to invest Rs 3,000 crore in the next five years to scale up its critical mineral extraction capacity, a top official of the company said. Attero Co-founder and CEO Nitin Gupta told PTI that the company plans to enhance total e-waste recycling capacity by over four times to 1 million tonnes in the next four years. "We are specifically looking to invest around Rs 3,000 crore in critical minerals facility expansion over the next five years. Roughly 40 per cent of that will go towards lithium, nickel, and if you read the scheme, within nickel, they have said they considered cobalt as well," he said. Attero claims to extract over 22 critical minerals, including gold, silver, copper, aluminum, nickel, lithium, cobalt and rare earths like neodymium, dysprosium, etc. "Our current capacity for electronic waste recycling is around 2,25,000 tonnes per annum. items.title: Rupee declines 23 paise to 92.85 against US dollar during early trade
items.rss_summary: The rupee saw heightened volatility and tumbled 23 paise to 92.85 against the US dollar in early trade on Monday, tracking a selling trend in domestic equity markets. Easing crude oil prices helped the local currency initially, but it soon came under pressure due to a firm American currency, forex traders said. At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 93.47 and climbed up to 92.43 before trading at 92.85 against the greenback, down 23 paise from its previous close. On Friday, the rupee sustained its ascending order for the fifth consecutive session to settle 70 paise higher at 92.62 against the US dollar. The unit reclaimed above the 93 level for the first time since April 10. The local unit has logged a sharp appreciation of over 1.6 per cent in the past five back-to-back sessions since the closing level of 94.19 against the greenback recorded on November 13.
